'''Zylan Anthony Cheatham''' (born November 17, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State Aztecs]] and the [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State Sun Devils]].

==Early life==
Cheatham grew up in [[South Phoenix]] and initially attended [[St. Mary's High School (Phoenix, Arizona)|St. Mary's High School]]. He transferred to [[South Mountain High School]] after his freshman year, playing basketball there for two seasons before transferring to [[Westwind Preparatory Academy]].<ref name="prominence"/> Cheatham transferred back to South Mountain after learning the school did not meet the NCAA's academic standards and retook all of his junior courses simultaneously with his senior courseload in order to graduate on time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2019/06/19/nba-draft-sleeper-zylan-cheatham-arizona-state-hidden-gem|title=Zylan Cheatham Is the NBA Draft's Hidden Gem|first=Kaelen|last=Jones|website=The Crossover|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]|date=June 19, 2019|access-date=July 28, 2019}}</ref> Ranked a consensus four star and top 100 recruit, Cheatham committed to [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] over offers from [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]], [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico]], [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]] and [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mwcconnection.com/2015/1/13/7540057/san-diego-state-basketball-4-star-freshman-power-forward-zylan-cheatham-will-redshirt-this-season|title=San Diego State Basketball: 4-star freshman power forward Zylan Cheatham will redshirt this season|first=Andrew|last=Bain|website=MWCConnection.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=January 13, 2015|access-date=July 28, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
===San Diego State Aztecs (2015–2017)===
Cheatham spent three seasons as a member of the [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State Aztecs]], [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his freshman season after breaking the fifth metatarsal in his left foot.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/2019/06/20/undrafted-asus-zylan-cheatham-agrees-deal-new-orleans-pelicans/1503209001/|title=Undrafted, ASU's Zylan Cheatham agrees to deal with New Orleans Pelicans|first=Jenna|last=Ortiz|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=June 20, 2019|access-date=July 28, 2019}}</ref> As a redshirt freshman in 2015–16, he averaged 7.9 points and 5.4 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mwcconnection.com/2016/10/5/13158650/san-diego-state-basketball-preview-2016|title=San Diego State basketball preview|first=Andy|last=Roberts|website=MWCConnection.com|date=October 5, 2016|access-date=July 27, 2019}}</ref> In his redshirt sophomore season in 2016–17, Cheatham averaged 9.1 points and 6.3 rebounds and was named honorable mention All-[[Mountain West Conference]]. He was named the Most Outstanding Player of the [[2016 Diamond Head Classic]] after averaging 15.7 points and 9.3 rebounds over four games as the Aztecs won the mid-season tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mcall.com/sd-sp-azhoops-20170410-story.html|title=Zylan Cheatham to transfer from SDSU|first=Mark|last=Zeigler|work=[[The Morning Call]]|date=April 14, 2017|access-date=July 28, 2019|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190728151314/https://www.mcall.com/sd-sp-azhoops-20170410-story.html|archive-date=July 28, 2019}}</ref> In April 2017, Cheatham announced that he would be leaving the program.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/19233889/arizona-state-lands-san-diego-state-forward-zylan-cheatham|title=San Diego State forward Zylan Cheatham transfers to Arizona State|first=Jeff|last=Goodman|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=April 24, 2017|access-date=July 27, 2019}}</ref>

===Arizona State Sun Devils (2018–2019)===
Cheatham transferred to [[Arizona State University]], citing a desire to play closer to home, but sat out the 2017–18 season due to NCAA transfer regulations.<ref name="prominence">{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/asu/2018/11/04/asu-basketball-zylan-cheatham-transfer-bobby-hurley/1618594002/|title=Zylan Cheatham ready to lead hometown ASU back to prominence|first=Michelle|last=Gardner|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=November 4, 2018|access-date=July 27, 2019}}</ref> He joined the [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Sun Devils]] for the 2018–19 season. Cheatham decided to wear jersey number 45 in reference to [[Michael Jordan]] who wore it during his comeback.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Eichenhofer |first1=Jim |title=Off the Court: Pelicans forward Zylan Cheatham |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/court-pelicans-forward-zylan-cheatham |website=NBA |access-date=September 2, 2026 |date=April 17, 2020}}</ref> He averaged 12.2 points and a [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]]-leading 10.3 rebounds per game. He was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and earned All-Defensive team honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/1871058/zylan-cheatham-asu-2018-19-all-pac-12-teams/|title=Cheatham, Dort lead list of ASU players on 2018–19 All-Pac-12 teams|website=[[KMVP-FM|ArizonaSports.com]]|date=March 11, 2019|access-date=July 27, 2019}}</ref> He was named Pac-12 player of the week on December 3, 2018, following the second [[triple double]] in ASU history after recording 14 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in an 83–71 win over [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/1758882/asus-zylan-cheatham-named-pac-12-player-of-the-week/|title=ASU's Zylan Cheatham named Pac-12 Player of the Week|website=[[KMVP-FM|ArizonaSports.com]]|date=December 3, 2018|access-date=July 28, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===New Orleans Pelicans (2019–2020)===
Cheatham participated in the [[NBA G League]] Elite Camp in May 2019.<ref>{{cite web|first=Eric|last=Sorenson|title=Cheatham Happy With Elite Camp Performance|url=https://www.sports360az.com/2019/05/cheatham-happy-with-elite-camp-performance/|website=Sports360AZ.com|date=May 14, 2019|access-date=July 28, 2019|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190517210447/https://www.sports360az.com/2019/05/cheatham-happy-with-elite-camp-performance/|archive-date=May 17, 2019}}</ref> After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], he was immediately offered a [[two-way contract]] by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] but his deliberation meant that the team instead gave it to his Sun Devils teammate [[Luguentz Dort]].<ref name=gardner>{{cite web |last1=Gardner |first1=Michelle |title=Former ASU basketball standout Zylan Cheatham giving back to community that groomed him |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/asu/2020/10/17/arizona-state-basketball-alum-zylan-cheatham-looking-give-back-community/3494620001/ |website=AZ Central |access-date=December 25, 2025 |date=October 17, 2020}}</ref> Cheatham joined the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]] and later signed a two-way contract with the Pelicans on July 24, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Cheatham and Gray to two-way contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-cheatham-and-gray-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 24, 2019|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref> Cheatham made his NBA debut on November 16, 2019,<ref>{{cite web|first=Jim|last=Eichenhofer|title=Behind the Numbers presented by HUB International: Warriors at Pelicans (11/17/19)|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/behind-numbers-presented-hub-international-warriors-pelicans-11/17/19|website=NBA.com|date=November 17, 2019|access-date=November 17, 2019}}</ref> in a 109–94 loss to the [[Miami Heat]], recording two points, three rebounds and one assist in 14 minutes of play.<ref>{{cite web |title=Heat 109-94 Pelicans (Nov 16, 2019) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401160820 |website=ESPN |access-date=19 June 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He spent the majority of the 2019–20 season in the NBA G League with the [[Birmingham Squadron|Erie BayHawks]].<ref name=realgm>{{cite web |title=Zylan Cheatham Player Profile, New Orleans Pelicans - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Zylan-Cheatham/Summary/52056 |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=19 June 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

===Iowa Wolves (2021)===
Cheatham was acquired by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] as part of a four-team trade on November 24, 2020, and his two-way contract was converted to a standard NBA contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquires George Hill, Zylan Cheatham, Josh Gray, Darius Miller, Kenrich Williams, One First and Two Second-Round Draft Picks and a Trade Exception|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/hill-cheatham-gray-miller-williams-201124|website=NBA.com|date=November 24, 2020|access-date=November 24, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder's Zylan Cheatham: Shipped to Thunder|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/thunders-zylan-cheatham-shipped-to-thunder/|website=CBSSports.com|publisher=RotoWire|date=November 22, 2020|access-date=November 24, 2020}}</ref> However, they waived him on December 2.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Waives Zylan Cheatham|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/cheatham-201202|website=NBA.com|date=December 2, 2020|access-date=December 2, 2020}}</ref>

On December 18, 2020, Cheatham signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign Zylan Cheatham|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-zylan-cheatham|website=NBA.com|date=December 19, 2020|access-date=September 25, 2021}}</ref> but was waived the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Waive Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-four-players|website=NBA.com|date=December 19, 2020|access-date=September 25, 2021}}</ref> He subsequently played for the [[Iowa Wolves]] in the [[2020–21 NBA G League season|G League hub season]] between February and March 2021.<ref>{{cite web|first=Randi|last=Burrell|title=Wolves Announce 2021 Roster|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-announce-2021-roster|website=NBA.com|date=January 25, 2021|access-date=September 25, 2021}}</ref>

In August 2021, Cheatham played for the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].<ref name="realgm" />

===Birmingham Squadron (2021–2022)===
On September 24, 2021, Cheatham signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for training camp.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans announce 2021 Training Camp information|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-announce-2021-training-camp-information|website=NBA.com|date=September 24, 2021|access-date=September 25, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on October 9<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans waive Cheatham and Harper, sign Banks and Hill|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-zylan-cheatham-jared-harper-sign-james-banks-malcolm-hill|website=NBA.com|date=October 9, 2021|access-date=October 9, 2021}}</ref> and subsequently joined the [[Birmingham Squadron]] for the [[2021–22 NBA G League season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron finalize roster for team's first training camp in Birmingham|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-squadron-announce-2021-training-camp-roster/|work=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}}</ref>

On December 22, 2021, Cheatham signed a 10-day contract with the [[Miami Heat]] via a COVID-related hardship exception.<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN ZYLAN CHEATHAM|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/press-release-zylan-cheatham-12212021|website=NBA.com|date=December 22, 2021|access-date=December 22, 2021}}</ref> Toward the end of his 10-day contract, with a huge outbreak on the team, Cheatham wound up testing positive for COVID as well.<ref>{{cite news |title=Zylan Cheatham Shares His Experience as 10-Day Replacement Player |url=https://www.slamonline.com/the-magazine/zylan-cheatham-shares-his-experience-as-a-10-day-replacement-player-in-the-nba/ |access-date=19 June 2025 |work=SLAM |date=14 January 2022 |language=en}}</ref> He did not appear in any games for the Heat during his tenure.<ref name=br2122>{{cite web |title=Zylan Cheatham 2021-22 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/cheatzy01/gamelog/2022/ |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=19 June 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

Cheatham re-joined the Squadron on January 3, 2022, but was removed from the team on January 6.<ref name=gleague-trans>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|title=NBA G League Transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220218010337/https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|archive-date=February 18, 2022}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2022)===
On January 12, 2022, Cheatham signed a 10-day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]] via another COVID-related hardship exception.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jazz Sign Zylan Cheatham to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-zylan-cheatham-10-day-contract |access-date=19 June 2025 |work=NBA.com |date=12 January 2022}}</ref> He played five minutes for the Jazz that night against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. It marked his only game for the Jazz.<ref name="br2122" /> On January 19, he was assigned to the Jazz's G League affiliate, the [[Salt Lake City Stars]]. He played two games for the Stars.<ref name="realgm" />

=== Return to Birmingham (2022–2023) ===
On January 24, 2022, Cheatham returned to the [[Birmingham Squadron]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Zylan Cheatham returns to the Birmingham Squadron|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/forward-zylan-cheatham-returns-to-the-birmingham-squadron/|website=NBA.com|date=January 24, 2022|access-date=January 25, 2022}}</ref> On February 4, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] via another COVID-related hardship exception.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pelicans sign Cheatham and Oni to 10-day contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-zylan-cheatham-miye-oni-10-day-contracts|access-date=February 4, 2022|website=NBA.com|date=February 4, 2022}}</ref> However, he didn't play a game for the team.<ref name="br2122" /> On February 14, Cheatham re-joined the Squadron once again.<ref name="gleague-trans" />

Cheatham joined the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Milwaukee Bucks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612749/bucks |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He re-joined the Squadron for the [[2022–23 NBA G League season]], but later parted ways on February 28, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=February 28, 2023|access-date=February 28, 2023}}</ref>

===Bayern Munich (2023)===
On March 6, 2023, Cheatham signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL) and the [[EuroLeague]] for the rest of the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Zylan Cheatham completes Bayern squad |url=https://fcbayern.com/basketball/en/news/2022-23/03/zylan-cheatham |access-date=19 June 2025 |work=fcbayern.com |date=6 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Bayern adds size with Zylan Cheatham {{!}} EuroLeague |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/bayern-adds-size-with-zylan-cheatham/ |access-date=19 June 2025 |work=Euroleague Basketball |date=6 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bayern registers Zylan Cheatham on the EuroLeague deadline |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1468997/zylan-cheatham-signs-with-bayern-euroleague/ |access-date=March 2, 2023 |website=Eurohoops |date=March 1, 2023}}</ref> In 19 BBL games, he averaged 8.8 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game. He also averaged 11.5 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.3 assists in six EuroLeague games.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zylan Cheatham, Basketball Player, News, Stats - australiabasket |url=https://basketball.australiabasket.com/player/Zylan-Cheatham/333305 |website=Eurobasket LLC |access-date=19 June 2025 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

===New Zealand Breakers (2023–2024)===
On July 18, 2023, Cheatham signed with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the [[2023–24 NBL season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maor: New Import Has A Special Level of Intensity |url=https://www.nzbreakers.basketball/news/maor-new-import-has-a-special-level-of-intensity |access-date=July 18, 2023 |website=nzbreakers.basketball |date=July 18, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Breakers lock in first import Zylan Cheatham ahead of NBL24|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nbl/story/_/id/37882517/nbl-new-zealand-breakers-sign-import-zylan-cheatham-ahead-nbl24|website=ESPN.com.au|access-date=July 18, 2023|date=June 20, 2023}}</ref> On October 27, 2023, he was ruled out for six to eight weeks with a fractured foot.<ref>{{cite web |title=Breakers cop big injury blow |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/breakers-cop-big-injury-blow |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=October 27, 2023 |date=October 27, 2023}}</ref> He returned to active status with the Breakers in late December, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zylan Cheatham, Will McDowell-White back for NZ Breakers' NBL clash with Sydney Kings |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/zylan-cheatham-will-mcdowell-white-back-for-nz-breakers-nbl-clash-with-sydney-kings/LQ3FH7Y7WNERDDZZ3R36VRYV5U/ |website=www.nzherald.co.nz |access-date=April 29, 2024 |date=December 19, 2023 |archive-date=April 29, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240429233025/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/zylan-cheatham-will-mcdowell-white-back-for-nz-breakers-nbl-clash-with-sydney-kings/LQ3FH7Y7WNERDDZZ3R36VRYV5U/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He averaged 15 points and seven rebounds per game for the Breakers.<ref name=nbl-june25>{{cite news |title=REPORT: Adelaide makes ANOTHER huge move |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/report-adelaide-makes-another-big-move |access-date=17 June 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=17 June 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

Cheatham played for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the [[2024 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Cheatham open to NBL return |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/cheatham-open-to-nbl-return |access-date=19 June 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=19 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

===Nagoya Diamond Dolphins (2024–2025)===
On August 1, 2024, Cheatham signed with [[Nagoya Diamond Dolphins]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nagoya-dolphins.jp/news/detail/id=18902|title=ザイラン・チータム選手 B.LEAGUE 2024-25 SEASON契約締結のお知らせ|language=ja|publisher=Nagoya Diamond Dolphins|date=August 1, 2024|access-date=August 20, 2024}}</ref> He averaged over 12 points, seven rebounds and three assists per game.<ref name="nbl-june25" />

===Adelaide 36ers (2025–present)===
On June 17, 2025, Cheatham signed with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] for the [[2025–26 NBL season]], returning to the league for a second stint.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cheatham joins 36ers |url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/cheatham-joins-36ers |access-date=17 June 2025 |work=Adelaide 36ers Official Website |date=17 June 2025}}</ref> On December 21, 2025, he re-signed with the 36ers for two more seasons.<ref>{{cite news |title=Adelaide 36ers re-sign athletic import Zylan Cheatham |url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/adelaide-36ers-re-sign-athletic-import-zylan-cheatham |access-date=21 December 2025 |work=Adelaide 36ers Official Website |date=21 December 2025}}</ref> He was named to the [[All-NBL Team|All-NBL Second Team]].<ref>{{cite news |title=League's best rewarded with All-NBL selection |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/leagues-best-rewarded-with-all-nbl-selection |access-date=23 February 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=23 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> In game four of the Championship Series against the [[Sydney Kings]], Cheatham recorded 23 points, nine assists, eight rebounds and two steals in a 92–91 win to level the series at 2–2.<ref>{{cite news |title=Adelaide in an epic: We're going to Game 5 |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/adelaide-sydney-game-4-report-championship-nbl |access-date=1 April 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=1 April 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Cheatham: 'Grit got us over the line' |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/grit-determination-and-instincts-power-36ers-to-victory |access-date=1 April 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=1 April 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Cheatham has 12 siblings.<ref name=gardner/> His brother, Wanyaa Stewart, was fatally shot on December 29, 2018, at a gas station in [[Tempe, Arizona]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nakamoto-White |first1=Ellie |title=Arrest made in killing of ASU basketball player's brother |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/tempe/2019/02/01/arrest-made-killing-asu-basketball-player-brother/2747288002/ |website=AZ Central |access-date=December 25, 2025 |date=February 1, 2019}}</ref>
